validity.recommendation: Correct Owner1/Operator from 'Transco' to 'Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America, LLC' (NGPL, a Kinder Morgan-affiliated system independent of Williams' Transco); consider whether this row belongs under the 'Transcontinental Gas Pipeline' GEM project cluster at all, since the physical facility is on NGPL's system, not Transco's.
validity.researcher_notes: The row's only existing ref (https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines, cited on every cell) is a generic EIA navigation page: url_verifier confirms it never names 'Transcontinental Gas Pipeline' or 'Sabine Pass' (name_found=false) and does not contain the Capacity/Diameter/SegmentCost values (200-but-value-absent on all three). Following the wiki's own citation pool for leads (Kinder Morgan/Williams cites) turned up nothing naming a Transco 'Sabine Pass Compression' project, so I searched open web for the project name directly. Two independent primary/secondary sources -- FERC's environmental assessment for Docket No. CP18-487 (govt regulator; https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/CP18-487-EA.pdf) and Natural Gas Intelligence trade press (https://web.archive.org/web/20240417181424/https://www.naturalgasintel.com/ngpl-seeks-swift-ferc-action-to-expand-sabine-pass-lng-service/) -- both independently identify the 'Sabine Pass Compression Project' (SPCP) as a project of Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America, LLC ('Natural'/NGPL), filed May 18, 2018, for a new 22,490-hp compressor station (CS 348) plus ~1,573 ft of 36-inch tie-in pipe in Cameron Parish, LA, to deliver 400,000 Dth/d (~400 MMcf/d) of firm capacity to Cheniere's Sabine Pass Liquefaction (SPL) terminal, planned in-service Q1 2020. NEITHER source mentions Transco, Williams, or Transcontinental Gas Pipeline anywhere -- this is a wholly separate FERC-regulated interstate system (NGPL, historically Kinder Morgan-affiliated) that happens to also serve the Sabine Pass LNG terminal, distinct from Transco's own (much larger, 1.2 MMDth/d) 2017 'Gulf Trace' project that ALSO serves Sabine Pass (cited on the same gem.wiki page, citation #18, Williams press release Feb 2017 -- that IS a genuine Transco project, but it is NOT this row: Gulf Trace's capacity, date, and cost don't match GEM's P2607 values, while NGPL's SPCP numbers match P2607's Capacity=400 MMcf/d and Diameter=36in exactly). The physical infrastructure described by P2607 (400 MMcf/d compression expansion feeding Sabine Pass, ~2020 in-service, 36-inch tie-in) is real, exists, and is correctly classified as an operating gas transmission expansion -- but it is NGPL's Sabine Pass Compression Project, not a Transco facility. This is very likely a citation/attribution mix-up on the wiki page (both Transco's Gulf Trace and NGPL's SPCP serve the same LNG terminal and share the generic 'Sabine Pass' name), which GEM appears to have inherited when building this row under the Transco pipeline cluster. Recommend the orchestrator re-home this row (or its Owner/Operator fields at minimum) to NGPL. Not flagging as 'duplicate' against the 37-row roster since no NGPL-attributed row exists in-scope to merge into; flagging as attribution/classification for human review instead. Opened all ~30 harvested wiki citations for this page's citation list and read the ones plausibly relevant to a Sabine Pass compression project (cites 4, 5, 9, 11, 12, 18, 34 and the FracTracker map cite 2); none of the wiki's own citations actually name this specific 400 MMcf/d compression project -- the wiki page bundles multiple Transco-system projects and the Sabine Pass Compression segment appears to have been added without its own dedicated citation, consistent with the misattribution.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost=$61,000,000 (USD) for this row, cited to the same generic EIA navigation URL that url_verifier confirms does not contain this figure ('200 but data value not found'). Neither of the two sources I found and verified (FERC EA for CP18-487; NGI trade press) states a total project cost -- the EA states only ancillary local-spending figures ($7.5M in construction payroll, $176,750 in property-tax-equivalent impact), not a capital cost for the project as a whole. I searched FERC's order-issuance materials (FERC's own docket search and news pages are Cloudflare-blocked to scripted access; tried Wayback captures of the FERC Glick-dissent news item and a general search for 'estimated cost' / 'total cost' + 'Sabine Pass Compression Project' -- no hit for a project-level cost figure in the sources that surfaced). $61,000,000 may be correct but I could not corroborate it from any source, primary or secondary -- treat as unverified rather than confirmed.
